model_assumptions.statement: Birth-order/cohort method captures delayed births and catch-up; ANU long-run judgement lowers the terminal rate from 1.62.
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Birth-order/cohort method captures delayed births and catch-up; ANU long-run judgement lowers the terminal rate from 1.62.

model_assumptions.statement: AGA reduces improvement rates because gains of 1930-1950 birth cohorts are not assumed to continue.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: ABS age-sex life tables plus revised AGA improvement factors; COVID adjustments through 2027-28
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: AGA reduces improvement rates because gains of 1930-1950 birth cohorts are not assumed to continue.

model_assumptions.statement: Long-run technical level matches 2021/2023 IGR and the Budget, close to a 20-year average; policy and foreign/domestic conditions remain dependencies.
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Long-run technical level matches 2021/2023 IGR and the Budget, close to a 20-year average; policy and foreign/domestic conditions remain dependencies.

model_assumptions.statement: Historical generational differences persist for future cohorts; composition and age-specific rates are separately modelled.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Cohort/lifecycle/age model retains historical generational differences
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Historical generational differences persist for future cohorts; composition and age-specific rates are separately modelled.

model_assumptions.statement: Underlying labour productivity converges to a technical long-run rate unchanged from 2023; diffusion, capital deepening and reform are not guaranteed.
model_assumptions.reference_period: convergence over around five years then long run
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Underlying labour productivity converges to a technical long-run rate unchanged from 2023; diffusion, capital deepening and reform are not guaranteed.

model_assumptions.statement: Domestic inflation stays at the RBA target midpoint; wages converge to 3.7% consistently with inflation and productivity.
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Domestic inflation stays at the RBA target midpoint; wages converge to 3.7% consistently with inflation and productivity.

model_assumptions.statement: Long-run anchor is a maintained price convention rather than a predicted sequence of future commodity shocks.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Bulk commodity prices decline to Budget anchors and then remain constant in real terms; terms of trade stay near 2027-28 level
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Long-run anchor is a maintained price convention rather than a predicted sequence of future commodity shocks.

model_assumptions.statement: Debt simulator and fiscal aggregation are internally coupled; long-run bond pricing is a technical closure.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Observed yield snapshot during forward estimates; 10-year AGS yield converges over 15 years to nominal GDP growth; tenors converge to historical relativities
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Debt simulator and fiscal aggregation are internally coupled; long-run bond pricing is a technical closure.

model_assumptions.statement: Tax receipts do not exceed the historical high; implicit future policy offsets nominal-threshold bracket creep. This is not a legislated perpetual ceiling.
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Tax receipts do not exceed the historical high; implicit future policy offsets nominal-threshold bracket creep. This is not a legislated perpetual ceiling.

model_assumptions.statement: Hospital/medical/pharmaceutical cost trends are estimated using a Tornqvist index and log-linear regression; coverage rebate differs.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Program-specific historical age-sex adjusted non-demographic cost-growth estimates; other health converges to historical GDP share then grows with health
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Hospital/medical/pharmaceutical cost trends are estimated using a Tornqvist index and log-linear regression; coverage rebate differs.

model_assumptions.statement: Updated service-use modelling separates cost pressures; demographic and non-demographic drivers both matter.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Separate residential/home care age-sex service models; historical exponential residential cost trend begins 2037-38
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Updated service-use modelling separates cost pressures; demographic and non-demographic drivers both matter.

model_assumptions.statement: Updated methodology and recent spending inform new participant/cost models; short scheme history limits extrapolation.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Budget reforms shape actuarial participant entries/exits; costs transition over five years to weekly earnings growth after medium term
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Updated methodology and recent spending inform new participant/cost models; short scheme history limits extrapolation.

model_assumptions.statement: Administrative base 2019-20 plus HILDA/SIH; accumulation and means-testing lower pension share while concessions grow.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: MARIA simulates assets/income and means-tested pensions; home/non-super savings imputed at retirement
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Administrative base 2019-20 plus HILDA/SIH; accumulation and means-testing lower pension share while concessions grow.

model_assumptions.statement: Adoption, complementary capital and reorganisation influence gains; task substitution and income distribution may offset fiscal effects.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: AI benefits inform the 1.2% productivity path; no separately identified central AI add-on
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Adoption, complementary capital and reorganisation influence gains; task substitution and income distribution may offset fiscal effects.

model_assumptions.statement: Energy buildout and adaptation depend on investment and delivery; four-damage climate model is explicitly partial.
model_assumptions.value_or_rule: Transport decarbonisation changes excise base; partial physical-damage paths are conditional comparisons, not full welfare estimates
model_assumptions.issuer_rationale: Energy buildout and adaptation depend on investment and delivery; four-damage climate model is explicitly partial.

Registration year differs from occurrence/cohort fertility; processing changes matter. Not terminal cohort fertility.
Quarter-end stock and revisions differ from annual IGR projections; no terminal population test.
A realised moving annual total is not the long-run technical level.
Trend is not Treasury annual structural rate; new Supplementary Survey methodology caveat retained.
PC uses ABS; cyclicality and revisions preclude treating one year as 40-year falsification. Page hours-growth discrepancy retained.

major_transitions.detail: Productivity scenarios and bounded fiscal illustration; labour/task, capital/investment and distribution channels mostly conditional. No separate additive AI coefficient.
Trade/investment/security pathways and historical indicators, not a single central-path fragmentation coefficient.
Quantitative partial climate-damage cases and excise path; energy resilience/reform framing is not an observed implementation outcome.
Demographic, participation and program-cost models; policy reform assumptions differ from empirical cost trends.
Sectoral composition projections/context; no standalone universal industrial-transformation shock.
Distribution, housing, taxes and trust discussion; no aggregate intergenerational equity score extracted.

limitations: Terminal fertility is retained as a model input, not duplicated as an observed outcome.
Productivity rate and tax ceiling are inputs, not independent output confirmations.
Employment level not separately extracted; labour-force size is not employment. Hours retained as the documented growth contribution and weekly employed-person measure.
No unsupported global/regional state or fiscal risk score.
Real GDP/GNI per-person units follow report conventions; do not directly subtract 2023 and 2026 real-dollar levels without a verified common price basis.
